summary: A plain <tr>. Hover is CSS-only; a row is not itself interactive. With `expansion`, it opens to show more under it: a disclosure button in its first cell, and a detail row across every column.
useWhen: every row, in either TableHead or TableBody

useInstead.when: the whole row should be clickable
useInstead.why: put the link or Button in a cell — nesting an interactive role on <tr> is not valid HTML

useInstead.when: the extra detail is long, has its own actions, or is read beside the list
useInstead.why: an expanded row pushes every row below it down; a panel beside the table keeps the list in place and can hold a form

selection.note: renders a leading Checkbox cell — a <th scope="col"> select-all inside TableHead, a <td> inside TableBody. Takes the checkbox's own props rather than a boolean, since a selectable row needs `checked`/`onChange` wiring. `useTableSelection`'s `headSelection` and `rowSelection` return exactly these props, tri-state header included

expansion.accepts: TableRowExpansion in TableBody, TableHeadExpansion in TableHead
expansion.note: in TableBody, `{ 'aria-label', content, isExpanded?, defaultExpanded?, onExpandedChange? }`: a leading cell with a disclosure button, and when open a second <tr> under the row whose one cell spans every column, counted from the row's own cells. In TableHead, `{ label }`: the header cell over the toggles, its name visually hidden, so the columns line up. Controlled with `isExpanded`, uncontrolled with `defaultExpanded`

guarantees: hover comes from CSS `:hover` plus a `data-hovered` escape hatch, not React Aria — a row takes no focus and fires no click, so there is no keyboard-versus-pointer distinction to track
the selection cell's element follows the section it sits in
an expandable row's toggle is a real <button> with `aria-expanded`, and `aria-controls` pointing at the detail row while it is open
closed points right and open points down — the shape carries the state as well as `aria-expanded`
the detail row spans every column, so it is read as one cell after its row
stripes count real rows only: an open detail takes its row's stripe and selection, and shifts nothing below it
requires: every row-selection Checkbox to be labelled — those boxes have no visible label by design, so see Checkbox's own contract
`isSelected` alongside a checked selection checkbox, so the row's state is not carried by colour alone
an `aria-label` on each expansion that names the row — "Details for run 4821" — not the action
notes: TableRow itself is never named — a <tr> is not an interactive element and takes no accessible name. The naming requirement above belongs to the Checkbox inside it.

antiPatterns.dont: hand-wiring the select-all's checked and indeterminate states
antiPatterns.why: the three states and "a partial header ticks to full" are easy to get subtly wrong, and every table needs the same logic
it takes no focus, so a keyboard user can never fire it
a checkbox that cannot be changed reads as broken rather than as disabled
the row is tinted with nothing announcing why
a column of buttons all named "Expand" gives a screen reader no way to tell which row it opens

antiPatterns.dont: a detail row you add yourself, with a colSpan you count by hand
antiPatterns.why: the hand count goes stale the day a column is added, and the detail then stops short or pushes the table wider

antiPatterns.dont: onClick on the row to expand it
antiPatterns.why: a row takes no focus, so a keyboard user can never open it; the toggle is a button with its state announced
